aac-to-mp3.q: Does AAC to MP3 reduce quality?
aac-to-mp3.a: Both are lossy, so transcoding AAC→MP3 loses a little detail. Use 256–320 kbps to keep it near-transparent. Convert for devices that don't support AAC/M4A.

aac-to-mp3.q: Why isn't my AAC playing everywhere?
aac-to-mp3.a: AAC (often in an .m4a wrapper) has excellent quality-per-byte, but some older or non-Apple devices prefer MP3.
No — temporary input/output, deleted after the download response.

add-attachment.q: What's the difference between an attachment and embedding?
add-attachment.a: An attachment is a file stored inside the PDF that the reader can open separately. Embedding means inlining content (images, fonts) into the page itself. Use attachments when you want recipients to access the supporting file but keep the visible PDF clean.

add-attachment.q: Will email clients flag attached PDFs as suspicious?
add-attachment.a: No, attachments inside a PDF aren't visible to email gateway scanners as separate attachments — the file is part of the PDF structure. Most spam filters don't flag them.

add-attachment.q: How big can the embedded file be?
add-attachment.a: Up to the 500 MB total file limit. The PDF size grows by approximately the embedded file's size.

add-hyperlinks.q: Can I link to other pages in the same PDF?
add-hyperlinks.a: Currently the tool supports external URLs. For internal page jumps, use the Bookmarks tool instead.

add-hyperlinks.q: Are the links visible to the user?
add-hyperlinks.a: The clickable rectangle is invisible by default. To add visible underlined link text, use the Edit PDF tool to draw the underline first.

add-hyperlinks.q: Will hyperlinks survive printing or PDF/A conversion?
add-hyperlinks.a: Hyperlinks don't print (they're interactive annotations) but they're preserved through most PDF/A conversions. PDF/A-1a strips them; PDF/A-2 keeps them.

add-shapes.q: Are shapes flattened into the page?
add-shapes.a: Yes — shapes become part of the page's content stream, not annotations. They can't be moved or deleted afterwards without re-editing the PDF.

add-shapes.q: Can I draw filled or only outlined shapes?
add-shapes.a: Both. Set fillColor for a filled shape; omit it and only the stroke renders. Set both for an outlined fill.
Use a color with alpha (e.g., rgba(255,0,0,0.5)) or pass an opacity value (0–1).

add-subtitles.q: Should I burn-in or use a soft subtitle track?
add-subtitles.a: Burn-in: best for social media (Twitter, Instagram) where players don't render subtitle tracks. Soft: best for accessibility — viewers can turn off.
Input: SRT. Burn-in output: works in any video player. Soft track: MP4 with WebVTT or MKV with SRT — depending on output format.

add-subtitles.q: Can I customize the font / size / color?
add-subtitles.a: Currently uses sensible defaults (white text with black outline, sans-serif). Custom styling is on the roadmap.

alternate-mix.a: The classic case is double-sided scanning on a single-sided scanner: scan the odd pages, flip the stack, scan the even pages in reverse, then alternate-mix them with reverse-alternate.

alternate-mix.q: What if the PDFs have different page counts?
alternate-mix.a: PrivaTools alternates pages until one source is exhausted, then appends the remaining pages from the longer source at the end.
No. Bookmarks from the originals are dropped because they would point to incorrect pages after interleaving.

annotate-pdf.a: By default no — they remain as editable annotations. If you want them permanently baked into the page, run the Flatten tool afterwards.
Yes. Add a note annotation with author + content; readers display it as an icon that opens a popup with the text on click.
Some do (text, highlight, square) but interactive ones (file attachments, popup notes) get flattened or stripped depending on the PDF/A profile.

audio-converter.a: Convert between MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, and AAC. The tool uses FFmpeg for professional-quality conversion with precise codec handling.
Yes. Available bitrates: 64k (small file), 128k (good), 192k (high quality), 256k (very high), and 320k (maximum). Default is 192k.

audio-converter.q: What is the file size limit?
audio-converter.a: Audio files up to 200 MB are supported. This covers most audio files including full albums in lossless FLAC format.

audio-merge.q: What if my files have different sample rates?
audio-merge.a: FFmpeg resamples to a common rate (usually 44.1 kHz) automatically. There may be a tiny re-encoding loss; for lossless concatenation use FLAC inputs.
No — files are concatenated seamlessly. To add silence, prepare it as a separate file with the same format and insert it in the order.
Practical limit is whatever fits inside the 500 MB output. Hours of MP3 at moderate bitrate is fine.

audio-trim.q: How precise are the start/end times?
audio-trim.a: To 1-second precision via stream-copy. For frame-accurate trimming, use the Trim Media tool which re-encodes.
No — we use stream-copy mode which preserves the original bytes. The trimmed file is identical quality to the source.
Same format as input. Trim an MP3 → get an MP3. Trim a FLAC → get a FLAC. No re-encoding.

auto-crop.q: Will this make text run off the page?
auto-crop.a: No — the algorithm leaves a small safety margin around detected content. If a page has no content (blank), the original MediaBox is kept.

auto-crop.q: What if my PDF has different page sizes after scanning?
auto-crop.a: Auto-crop computes the bounding box per-page, so pages are independently cropped to their own content.
After auto-crop, printing produces a smaller paper size. If you need the same paper size with less margin, use the Resize tool afterwards.

avi-to-mp4.a: AVI is an old Microsoft container with poor support for modern codecs and metadata. MP4 is the universal standard — every modern device, browser, and editor plays it.

avi-to-mp4.q: What if my AVI uses DivX or Xvid?
avi-to-mp4.a: FFmpeg re-encodes the video to H.264 inside the MP4 container, so any source codec is handled.

avi-to-mp4.q: Will the file get bigger or smaller?
avi-to-mp4.a: Usually similar or smaller. Old AVIs often used inefficient codecs; modern H.264 typically achieves the same quality at a smaller size.

avi-to-webm.a: To turn an old AVI clip into a small, web-ready, open-format video. WebM (VP9/Opus) re-encodes the AVI for efficient browser playback.
Usually significantly — modern WebM is far more efficient than typical legacy AVI codecs.
Yes — local FFmpeg conversion; files deleted after the response.

base64.q: Can I encode files (not just text)?
base64.a: Yes. Upload any file — images, PDFs, binaries — and the tool returns the Base64-encoded string. Useful for embedding files in JSON, HTML, or CSS.

base64.q: Is there a size limit for encoding?
base64.a: Files up to 500 MB can be encoded. Keep in mind that Base64 output is approximately 33% larger than the original file.
Standard Base64 (RFC 4648) using A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, and /. URL-safe Base64 (replacing + and / with - and _) is also available.

batch-compress-pdf.q: How many PDFs can I upload?
batch-compress-pdf.a: Up to 50 files per batch, up to 500 MB per file.
Yes — the backend runs 4 worker processes simultaneously, so 4 files compress at once. Total time scales nearly linearly with file count divided by 4.

batch-compress-pdf.q: What's the difference between Light, Recommended, and Extreme?
batch-compress-pdf.a: Light shrinks structure only (5–30% reduction, no visible quality loss). Recommended (default) resamples images at 150 DPI (40–70% reduction). Extreme drops to 96 DPI and lower JPEG quality (60–90% reduction).

bates-numbering.a: Sequential page identification across legal discovery documents. Each page in a production gets a unique identifier so attorneys can reference exact pages.

bates-numbering.q: Can I start the numbering at a value other than 1?
bates-numbering.a: Yes — set start_number to any positive integer. This is the standard workflow for continuing a numbering scheme across multiple production batches.
Yes — Bates numbers are stamped directly onto the page content, so they remain after redaction (unless the redaction rectangle covers them).

bmp-to-jpg.a: BMP files are uncompressed and can be 10–50× larger than the same image as JPG. Converting saves enormous space with virtually no visible quality difference for photos.
For screenshots and pixel art, consider BMP to PNG instead — PNG is lossless and handles sharp edges better than JPG.
Yes. All standard BMP variants (1-bit, 4-bit, 8-bit, 16-bit, 24-bit, 32-bit, RLE-compressed) are supported.

bmp-to-pdf.q: Why is the output PDF so much smaller than the BMPs?
bmp-to-pdf.a: BMP is uncompressed; PDF stores images in DCT (JPEG) or Flate format. A 5 MB BMP usually becomes a few hundred KB inside the PDF.
By default the conversion is near-lossless using high-quality JPEG. For 100% lossless, convert via PNG first (PNG-to-PDF) — slightly larger output.

bmp-to-pdf.q: How many BMPs can I convert at once?
bmp-to-pdf.a: Up to the 500 MB total file limit. Several dozen images is routine.

bmp-to-png.a: PNG is lossless like BMP but uses compression — typically 70–90% smaller files. PNG is also the standard format for web and modern software.
Yes — pixel-perfect identical. PNG uses lossless compression, so no pixel data changes.
Supported. 1-bit, 4-bit, and 8-bit palette BMPs convert to indexed-color PNGs preserving the original palette.

booklet-pdf.q: Why is the order so strange?
booklet-pdf.a: Saddle-stitch binding folds the sheets in half — the front cover of sheet 1 carries pages 8 and 1, the back carries pages 2 and 7. The math is fixed by binding geometry.

booklet-pdf.q: What if my page count isn't a multiple of 4?
booklet-pdf.a: PrivaTools pads with blank pages at the end before computing the imposition order, so the booklet always works.

booklet-pdf.q: Can I use this for thick books?
booklet-pdf.a: Saddle-stitch caps at about 80 pages (20 sheets) because the inner pages start to creep. For longer documents use perfect binding (no imposition needed).

bookmarks.q: Can I create a multi-level bookmark tree?
bookmarks.a: Yes. You can nest bookmarks under parent entries to create a hierarchical table of contents with multiple levels.

bookmarks.q: Do bookmarks work in all PDF readers?
bookmarks.a: Yes. The bookmarks use the standard PDF outline format supported by Adobe Reader, Preview, Chrome, Firefox, and all major PDF viewers.

bookmarks.q: Can I import a bookmark structure from a text file?
bookmarks.a: Currently, bookmarks are created manually in the editor. You can copy-paste titles and set page numbers individually.

case-converter.a: 12: lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title Case, Sentence case, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, CONSTANT_CASE, dot.case, path/case, and iNVERSE.

case-converter.q: Will it handle existing camelCase or snake_case input correctly?
case-converter.a: Yes. The tool detects word boundaries from underscores, hyphens, spaces, and lowercase→uppercase transitions, so converting between any two cases works correctly.

case-converter.q: Does it run in my browser?
case-converter.a: Yes — 100%. Your text never leaves the page. Useful for renaming variables, generating CSS class names, or normalizing identifiers without exposing them to a server.

chat-with-pdf.q: Where does my PDF go when I chat with it?
chat-with-pdf.a: Nowhere near PrivaTools. The text is extracted by pdf.js inside your browser tab, and each question is sent, together with that text, directly from your browser to the AI provider you picked, authenticated with your own API key. Open DevTools → Network and you will see requests only to that provider.

chat-with-pdf.q: Which AI providers can I use?
chat-with-pdf.a: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, or any self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as Ollama or vLLM. You paste your own key once; it is stored encrypted on this device and never sent to PrivaTools.

chat-with-pdf.q: Why do I need my own API key?
chat-with-pdf.a: A conversational answer needs a full LLM, and proxying documents through our server would break the privacy model — we would see them. Bring-your-own-key means you pay your provider directly (typically fractions of a cent per question) and your document bypasses us entirely.

chat-with-pdf.q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
chat-with-pdf.a: Not directly — a scan has no text layer. Run OCR PDF first, download the searchable PDF, then chat with that. The tool tells you when it finds no extractable text.

chat-with-pdf.q: How long a document can it handle?
chat-with-pdf.a: About 100,000 characters (roughly 50–70 pages of dense text) are sent as context per question. For longer documents the beginning is used and the assistant is told so — asking about specific sections or splitting the PDF first gives better answers.

chat-with-pdf.q: Are my questions or the answers stored anywhere?
chat-with-pdf.a: PrivaTools stores nothing — the conversation lives only in your browser tab. Your AI provider handles the request under its own API terms, the same as any other API call made with your key.

color-converter.a: Yes — paste #RRGGBBAA or rgba(...) and the alpha channel is preserved across all output formats.

color-converter.q: Why does my CMYK look different from print?
color-converter.a: CMYK conversion uses a sRGB → CMYK approximation. For exact print color, use your printer's color profile.
Yes — pure browser JavaScript. No network requests.

compare-pdf.q: Does this work on scanned PDFs?
compare-pdf.a: Only with OCR. Run OCR PDF on both files first so the text layer is present, then compare.

compare-pdf.q: How accurate is the text diff?
compare-pdf.a: Word-level diff handles reordering, insertion, deletion, and formatting changes. Diffs based on character runs would be noisier.

compare-pdf.q: Can I compare more than two files?
compare-pdf.a: Run Compare twice (A vs B, then B vs C) to chain a multi-revision comparison.

compress-pdf.q: How much smaller will my PDF actually get?
compress-pdf.a: Most PDFs shrink 50–75%. Scanned PDFs with large embedded images often see 70–90% reduction; text-heavy PDFs with vector graphics may only shrink 5–15% because the text is already minimally encoded.

compress-pdf.q: Will I lose quality when I compress?
compress-pdf.a: Text and vector graphics are always lossless — you cannot tell them apart from the original. Only embedded raster images are recompressed, and only at the Recommended or Extreme presets. Use the Light preset to keep images untouched.

compress-pdf.q: Is it safe to upload a sensitive PDF here?
compress-pdf.a: Yes. The compressed file is processed in an isolated Docker container, held in temporary per-request storage for the duration of the request, and unlinked the moment the response is delivered. The file is never written to permanent storage, never logged, and never used to train any model. The entire stack is open source so you can verify this on GitHub.

500 MB per file. There is no daily, weekly, or monthly quota — you can compress unlimited files. If you need to compress dozens of files at once, use the Batch Compress PDF tool which accepts up to 50 PDFs in one go.

compress-pdf.q: Can I compress a password-protected PDF?
compress-pdf.a: Not directly — encryption prevents the compressor from rewriting the content streams. Use the Unlock PDF tool first (you'll need the password), compress the unlocked version, then re-protect with the Protect PDF tool if needed.

compress-pdf.q: How is this different from iLovePDF or Smallpdf?
compress-pdf.a: Free with no daily quota (iLovePDF and Smallpdf cap free tier at 2 files/day), no watermark, no account required, no file size limit beyond 500 MB, and the entire compressor is open source under the MIT license so you can self-host it.

compress-video.q: How much can a video be compressed?
compress-video.a: Typical results are 30-70% size reduction at Medium compression. Raw or high-bitrate videos see the largest savings.

compress-video.q: Does compression change the video resolution?
compress-video.a: No. The resolution stays the same by default. Only the bitrate is reduced. You can optionally lower the resolution for even smaller files.
The output is MP4 with H.264 encoding, which is universally compatible with all devices and browsers.

create-zip.a: Not yet. Create ZIP currently produces standard unencrypted ZIP archives; password-protected ZIP creation is on the roadmap.
Uploaded files are placed at the root of the archive. To preserve a folder structure, upload them folder-by-folder using the multi-folder option.

create-zip.q: What compression level should I choose?
create-zip.a: Balanced is best for most files. Store is fastest for already-compressed files like JPG, MP4, and PDF. Maximum can shrink text-heavy files more but takes longer.

cron-parser.q: Does it support Quartz cron with seconds?
cron-parser.a: No. This tool intentionally supports standard 5-field cron because that is what Linux crontab, many schedulers, and most deployment platforms use.

cron-parser.q: Which timezone is used for next runs?
cron-parser.a: Your browser's local timezone. The expression itself is not uploaded or evaluated on the server.

cron-parser.q: Can it validate ranges and steps?
cron-parser.a: Yes. It catches invalid ranges, bad steps, out-of-bounds values, and expressions with the wrong number of fields.

crop-pdf.a: Crop uses your manual margins (same on every page). Auto-Crop detects each page's actual content bounding box automatically.

crop-pdf.q: Will the cropped content be deleted from the file?
crop-pdf.a: No — only the visible region changes. The full page content is still in the file. To permanently remove the cropped data, run Flatten or Sanitize afterwards.

crop-pdf.q: How do I undo a crop?
crop-pdf.a: Re-open the PDF in PrivaTools Crop with negative margins to expand the box, or run Flatten which bakes the current crop in.

csv-json.a: Standard RFC 4180: commas in values must be quoted; quotes inside values are doubled (""). PrivaTools handles both.
Nested objects are flattened to dot-notation columns (user.name, user.email) for CSV output. Reverse direction reconstructs the nesting.
No — pure-browser conversion. No data leaves your machine.

csv-to-pdf.a: Yes. Comma, semicolon, tab, and pipe delimiters are automatically detected. You can also specify the delimiter manually.
Wide tables can be rendered in landscape orientation. If they still exceed the page width, columns are scaled to fit or split across pages.

csv-to-pdf.q: Is the first row treated as a header?
csv-to-pdf.a: By default yes — the first row is bolded as a header. You can disable this if your data has no header row.

delete-annotations.q: Will this remove form fields too?
delete-annotations.a: Yes — form fields are a type of annotation. To preserve form structure but clear values, use the Fill Form tool with empty values instead.
Yes — hyperlinks are link annotations. Use this to make a PDF completely 'read-only' as a static document.
Yes, signature annotations are removed too — which invalidates the cryptographic signature.

delete-pages.q: What happens to bookmarks pointing to deleted pages?
delete-pages.a: They're either dropped or rewritten to the nearest remaining page, depending on outline structure. The Bookmarks tool can be used afterwards to clean them up.
Yes — use ranges like '5-12'. Mix single pages and ranges freely.
Visible page numbers (added with the Page Numbers tool) stay as they were rendered. The internal page indices reflect the new order.

deskew-pdf.q: My scans look fine — should I run deskew?
deskew-pdf.a: If the text appears tilted by more than ~0.5°, deskew helps OCR accuracy noticeably. For perfectly straight scans it's a no-op.
Yes — rotated pages need a slightly larger canvas. PrivaTools fills the margins with the surrounding background color (usually white).

deskew-pdf.q: Should I deskew before or after OCR?
deskew-pdf.a: Always before. OCR engines are much more accurate on straight-line text.

edit-pdf.q: Can I edit the existing text in a PDF?
edit-pdf.a: The editor supports adding new text, shapes, highlights, and freehand drawings on top of the page. Direct editing of existing text glyphs requires re-authoring the document because PDF stores text as positioned glyphs, not as flowing paragraphs.

Yes. When you save, annotations are flattened into the PDF so they appear identically in every viewer (Adobe Reader, Preview, Chrome, mobile readers) and cannot be removed by toggling annotation visibility.
Text boxes, freehand pen, highlighter, rectangles, circles, lines, and arrows. You can set color, opacity, line thickness, and font size for each. Move and resize freely before saving.

edit-pdf.q: Is it safe to edit a confidential PDF here?
edit-pdf.a: Yes. The PDF is held in temporary per-request storage inside an isolated Docker container only for the duration of your edit session — both input and output are unlinked the moment your download begins. No copy remains in permanent storage, logs, or backups. The editor code is open source under MIT for verification.
500 MB per file with no daily or monthly quota. There is no page-count cap; very long PDFs render page-by-page as you scroll.

edit-pdf.q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
edit-pdf.a: No. No account, no email, no sign-up. The editor loads directly in your browser; the privacy guarantees come from the architecture, not from a user profile.

edit-pdf.q: How is this different from Adobe Acrobat or PDFescape?
edit-pdf.a: Free with no daily limit (PDFescape caps free use at 10 MB / 100 pages, Adobe requires a paid subscription for full editing), no account required, and the entire editor is open source so you can self-host it. We don't store your file or send it to any third-party API.

env-validator.a: No. It is a fast syntax and hygiene check. Use dedicated secret scanning before committing any real credentials.

env-validator.q: Will it reveal my secrets to PrivaTools?
env-validator.a: No. The .env text stays in browser memory and is never sent to the backend.
Missing equals signs, invalid variable names, duplicate keys, empty values, unquoted spaces, and short-looking secret values.

epub-to-pdf.a: Yes. Chapter headings, bold/italic text, embedded images, and basic CSS styling are preserved in the PDF output.
No. DRM-protected e-books cannot be converted. The tool only works with DRM-free EPUB files.

epub-to-pdf.q: What page size options are available?
epub-to-pdf.a: A4, Letter, and custom dimensions. The text is reflowed to fit the chosen page size while keeping chapter breaks.

esign-pdf.q: Is this a cryptographically valid signature?
esign-pdf.a: No — this places a visual signature image, like signing paper. For cryptographically verifiable signatures, use the Sign PDF tool with a certificate.

esign-pdf.q: Does my signature image stay on PrivaTools?
esign-pdf.a: No. It's used only to render the output PDF and is deleted immediately afterwards.

esign-pdf.q: Can I use a signature image I already have?
esign-pdf.a: Yes — upload a transparent PNG of your signature instead of drawing one.

excel-to-pdf.a: No — only computed values appear. The formulas themselves are not included (PDF has no formula concept).
Charts render as static images. Embedded images are preserved at their original size.

excel-to-pdf.q: How does it handle very wide sheets?
excel-to-pdf.a: Wide sheets paginate across multiple PDF pages, with column headers repeated on each.

extract-archive.a: Password-protected archives are not supported yet. Extract Archive currently handles unencrypted ZIP and TAR-family archives; encrypted archive support is on the roadmap.
No. Extract Archive currently supports ZIP and TAR-family archives (.tar, .tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz). RAR and 7z support is on the roadmap.

extract-archive.q: What if the archive contains many small files?
extract-archive.a: Up to 1000 files per archive. For larger, split before zipping.

extract-audio.a: WAV/FLAC are lossless. MP3/AAC at 192 kbps+ is transparent for most listeners. Lower bitrates lose quality.

extract-audio.q: What if the video has multiple audio tracks?
extract-audio.a: PrivaTools extracts the first/default audio track. Multi-track extraction is on the roadmap.

extract-audio.q: Can I extract just a section of the audio?
extract-audio.a: Use Trim Media first to isolate the section, then extract audio from the trimmed video.

extract-images.q: Will the images be the original resolution?
extract-images.a: Yes. PDF embeds images at the resolution set when the PDF was created — extraction recovers them unchanged.

extract-images.q: What if the same image appears multiple times?
extract-images.a: Each visual occurrence is extracted, even if it's the same underlying image data. Use deduplication after if needed.

extract-images.q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
extract-images.a: Yes — each page of a scanned PDF is one big image. The tool extracts that page-image directly.

extract-pages.q: How is this different from Delete Pages?
extract-pages.a: Extract keeps the listed pages; Delete removes them. They're complementary — use whichever produces less typing.

extract-pages.q: Can I extract pages into separate files?
extract-pages.a: For one-file-per-page splitting, use the Split PDF tool with 'individual' mode.
Bookmarks pointing to kept pages are preserved; those pointing to dropped pages are removed.

extract-tables.a: CSV, Excel (.xlsx), and JSON. Each table is extracted separately and all results are packaged in a ZIP file.

extract-tables.q: Can it extract tables from scanned PDFs?
extract-tables.a: For best results, run OCR first using the OCR tool to create a text layer, then use table extraction. The tool works best with text-based PDFs.

extract-tables.q: How does the tool detect table boundaries?
extract-tables.a: It uses Camelot and Tabula libraries, which detect ruled lines and text alignment patterns to identify table structures. Tables without visible borders may need manual page selection.

fill-form.q: How do I know what the form field names are?
fill-form.a: Use the /api/fill-form/fields endpoint (or paste-then-inspect): PrivaTools returns the list of field names, types, and current values without filling anything.

fill-form.q: Can I flatten the filled form?
fill-form.a: Yes — run the Flatten tool afterwards to bake the values into the page content so they can't be edited.

fill-form.q: Does this work on signed forms?
fill-form.a: Filling a signed form invalidates the signature. Sign last, after filling.

flac-to-mp3.q: Will I lose quality converting FLAC to MP3?
flac-to-mp3.a: Yes — FLAC is lossless and MP3 is lossy, so the conversion discards some audio data. At 256–320 kbps the difference is inaudible to most people, but it's a one-way trade for a smaller, universally-compatible file.

flac-to-mp3.q: Why convert FLAC to MP3 at all?
flac-to-mp3.a: MP3 plays on virtually every device and is roughly 3–6× smaller than FLAC — ideal for phones, portable players, and sharing.
No. Uploads and outputs are temporary and removed right after the download.

flatten-pdf.q: What does flattening a PDF mean?
flatten-pdf.a: Flattening converts interactive elements like form fields, annotations, and layers into static page content. The visual appearance stays the same but the elements can no longer be edited.

flatten-pdf.q: When should I flatten a PDF?
flatten-pdf.a: Flatten before sharing filled forms (to prevent edits), before printing (to avoid rendering issues), or when a recipient's PDF viewer does not display annotations correctly.
Sometimes. Removing form field metadata and annotation data can slightly reduce file size, but the effect depends on the document.

flip-image.q: Horizontal vs vertical — when do I use which?
flip-image.a: Horizontal flip mirrors left↔right — the most common use is fixing selfies that come out mirrored. Vertical flip turns the image upside down — used for design layouts or correcting scans that were placed face-down.

flip-image.q: Does flipping change the file size?
flip-image.a: Effectively no — flipping is a pure pixel rearrangement, so the encoded output is similar in size to the input (sometimes 1-3% larger because compression heuristics work slightly differently on the new orientation).
We strip EXIF orientation hints on save, so the saved image bytes match what you see. If you need the original metadata kept, use Remove EXIF + this tool together.

form-creator.q: What field types can I add?
form-creator.a: Text inputs, text areas, checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns, date pickers, and signature fields.

form-creator.q: Will the form work in Adobe Reader?
form-creator.a: Yes. The forms use the standard AcroForm format, which is compatible with Adobe Reader, Foxit, and all major PDF viewers.

form-creator.q: Can I set fields as required?
form-creator.a: Yes. Mark any field as required to prevent submission without filling it in. You can also set validation rules like numeric-only or email format.

generate-barcode.q: What barcode type for a URL?
generate-barcode.a: Use QR code — barcodes like Code 128 work for text but are much wider for the same content.
Yes — barcodes are rendered at the standard 2D module size. Printed at 100% on a regular printer, any standard scanner reads them.

generate-barcode.q: Can I include a check digit?
generate-barcode.a: EAN-13 and UPC-A auto-calculate the check digit. Code 128 has a built-in checksum. Code 39 supports optional checksums.

generate-favicon.q: Do I need all those sizes?
generate-favicon.a: Yes — different browsers and devices use different sizes (16×16 for tabs, 192×192 for Android home screen, 512×512 for PWA install).

generate-favicon.q: Should I use PNG or SVG source?
generate-favicon.a: SVG is best — it stays sharp at every size. PNG works if you only have a raster logo. JPG loses some sharpness from compression.
No — favicons render exactly as uploaded. To get a circular look, upload a circular PNG with transparency.

gif-to-jpg.a: Only the first frame is converted. To extract every frame as JPGs, use a dedicated GIF frame extractor — coming soon to PrivaTools.
No — JPG doesn't support transparency. Transparent pixels in the source GIF become white in the JPG.

gif-to-jpg.q: Why convert GIF to JPG anyway?
gif-to-jpg.a: GIFs are limited to 256 colors and can be larger than JPGs of the same single frame. JPG is ideal when you only need a static still and want smaller file size.

gif-to-mp4.a: MP4 is dramatically smaller (better compression), supports audio, and plays smoother. Most social platforms now auto-convert uploaded GIFs to MP4 anyway.

gif-to-mp4.q: Will the loop work in MP4?
gif-to-mp4.a: MP4 doesn't have built-in loop info — players decide. Embed with <video loop autoplay muted> to mimic GIF behavior on the web.
MP4 doesn't support transparency. Transparent pixels render against a black background. Use WebM with VP9 if you need alpha.

gif-to-pdf.q: Do animated GIFs animate inside the PDF?
gif-to-pdf.a: No — PDF doesn't support animation. Only the first frame is used. To convert animation to PDF, use GIF to MP4 then Video to PDF for keyframes.
GIF transparent pixels render against a white page background. Use PNG-to-PDF if you need true alpha.

gif-to-pdf.q: Can the GIF stay as a GIF inside the PDF?
gif-to-pdf.a: PDF doesn't natively support GIF — the image is re-encoded as JPEG or Flate during embedding.

gif-to-png.a: Only the first frame is converted to PNG. For animated GIFs, consider converting to a video format like MP4 or WebM using our GIF to MP4 tool.
Yes — PNG fully supports transparency, so transparent areas of the GIF come through cleanly.
Yes. Both GIF and PNG are lossless formats, so the first frame is reproduced pixel-perfectly.

gitignore-generator.q: Does it call the toptal/gitignore API?
gitignore-generator.a: No. The templates are bundled in the app so the generator works offline and does not leak your selected stack.
Yes. Select any combination and the generated .gitignore groups each template under a comment header.

gitignore-generator.q: Can I download the file directly?
gitignore-generator.a: Yes. You can copy the text or download a .gitignore file from the browser.

graphql-formatter.q: Does it need my GraphQL schema?
graphql-formatter.a: No. The formatter only structures the query text and does not introspect or validate against a schema.

graphql-formatter.q: Can it format mutations and fragments?
graphql-formatter.a: Yes. Queries, mutations, fragments, arguments, arrays, and nested selection sets are handled.
Yes. The GraphQL text is formatted locally in your browser.

grayscale-pdf.a: Yes — the text layer is preserved. Only the rendered visuals change to grayscale.
Cheaper printing on black-and-white printers, smaller file size, accessibility for color-blind readers, archival storage.

grayscale-pdf.q: How does this differ from black-and-white?
grayscale-pdf.a: Grayscale preserves shading (256 grey levels). True black-and-white (1-bit) is harsher but smaller — not currently offered as a separate option.

hash-generator.a: For non-security purposes (file integrity, deduplication): yes. For security (passwords, signatures): no — MD5 is broken. Use SHA-256 or SHA-512.
Verifying file integrity after download, deduplication, change detection, content-addressed storage.

hash-generator.q: Is the hash calculation done in the browser?
hash-generator.a: Yes — Web Crypto API runs the hash in your browser. Files are not uploaded.

header-footer.q: Will the header/footer overlap existing content?
header-footer.a: It might if your pages have content close to the edges. Use the Crop or Resize tool first to add margin space if needed.

header-footer.q: Can I exclude the cover page?
header-footer.a: Pages-to-affect parameter accepts ranges like '2-' to skip the first page or '2-N-1' to skip first + last.

header-footer.q: Are these editable annotations or baked-in?
header-footer.a: Baked into the page content. They can't be removed without re-editing — use Whiteout to cover them if needed later.

heic-to-jpg.q: Why can't I open HEIC files on my computer?
heic-to-jpg.a: HEIC is Apple's default photo format since iOS 11. Windows and many web apps do not support it natively. Converting to JPG makes the images universally compatible.

heic-to-jpg.q: Is image quality lost during conversion?
heic-to-jpg.a: At quality 90-100, the difference is imperceptible. Lower quality settings reduce file size with minimal visible degradation.
Yes. Camera data, GPS location, and orientation are preserved by default. Use the Remove EXIF tool afterward if you want to strip metadata.

heic-to-pdf.q: Will the PDF be much larger than the HEIC?
heic-to-pdf.a: Yes — HEIC is more efficient than JPEG. The PDF uses JPEG internally and is typically 2-3x the size of the source HEICs.
Default JPEG quality is 90, which is visually indistinguishable. Lossless would require PNG-to-PDF and produce much larger files.
Stripped during conversion. Use View EXIF first if you want to record GPS coordinates before they're gone.

heic-to-png.q: What's HEIC and why convert it?
heic-to-png.a: HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) is Apple's image format from iOS 11 onward. It's space-efficient but not widely supported outside Apple's ecosystem. PNG works everywhere.

heic-to-png.q: Is PNG better than JPG for HEIC conversion?
heic-to-png.a: If you need transparency or are doing further editing: yes. For sharing on the web or attaching to emails: JPG is fine and 3–5x smaller.
Most are stripped during conversion (since PNG and HEIC have different metadata formats). If you need to preserve EXIF, use HEIC to JPG instead and the standard EXIF block survives.

highlight-pdf.q: Are the highlights real PDF annotations or flattened images?
highlight-pdf.a: Real PDF annotations. They render in every PDF viewer and can be removed later if you reopen the file in an editor. Nothing about the underlying text is changed.

highlight-pdf.q: Can I highlight multiple phrases at once?
highlight-pdf.a: Run the tool once per phrase. Each run preserves previous highlights, so you can layer different colors for different keywords.
Toggle case-sensitive matching for exact-case search; leave it off for case-insensitive flexible matching. Case-insensitive is the default.

html-to-pdf.q: Can I convert a live website URL to PDF?
html-to-pdf.a: Yes. Enter any public URL and the server will render the page — including CSS, images, and JavaScript — and convert it to PDF.
Yes. A headless browser executes JavaScript before capturing the page, so dynamically loaded content appears in the PDF.

html-to-pdf.q: Are external stylesheets and images included?
html-to-pdf.a: Yes. The renderer fetches external CSS, web fonts, and images. Only resources behind authentication may not load.

image-compressor.a: Yes — PNG compression here is lossless. The pixels are byte-identical to the original; only the encoding is optimized via zlib levels and palette reduction. Verify with `cmp` or a pixel-diff tool: zero difference.

image-compressor.q: How much can I expect a JPG to shrink?
image-compressor.a: JPGs typically shrink 40–70% at quality 75 with no visible difference for photos. Screenshots and graphics with flat colors shrink more aggressively. Quality 60 still looks good on most photos and gets you 60–80% reduction.

image-compressor.q: Will compression strip my EXIF / GPS data?
image-compressor.a: By default EXIF is preserved. If you want to strip it (for privacy when sharing photos), use the dedicated Remove EXIF tool after compressing — or use Strip Metadata for a one-step solution.

image-compressor.q: Can I batch-compress dozens of images?
image-compressor.a: Yes. Drop as many as you want; each is compressed with the same settings, then bundled into a single ZIP. There is no daily cap on the number of files.

image-compressor.q: Is it safe to compress photos with sensitive content?
image-compressor.a: Yes. Each image is held in temporary per-request storage only for the duration of the request, then unlinked. No image is written to permanent storage, none is logged, and none is used to train any model. The codec runs server-side in an isolated container; the entire codebase is open source for verification.

image-compressor.q: How is this different from TinyPNG or Squoosh?
image-compressor.a: TinyPNG caps free use at 20 images/month and uploads to their servers. Squoosh is browser-only but doesn't support batch. PrivaTools is unlimited, batch-friendly, server-processed for speed on large files, and the server-side code is self-hostable so you can run it on your own infrastructure.

image-converter.q: Which format is best for what?
image-converter.a: PNG for graphics with transparency or crisp text/UI elements. JPG for photos (smaller files at near-identical quality). WebP for web delivery (smaller than JPG at the same quality, supported by all modern browsers). TIFF for archival or print workflows. HEIC for iPhone-style storage (limited compatibility outside Apple). AVIF for cutting-edge web (smallest of all, but newer browsers only).

EXIF is stripped during conversion by default for privacy (GPS, camera model, timestamps removed). Use View EXIF first to record any metadata you want to keep, or use the 'preserve metadata' toggle in advanced options if your destination workflow needs the original EXIF.

Yes — upload multiple images and all are converted to the chosen format, then bundled into a ZIP. For format-specific batch workflows you can also use the dedicated tools (jpg-to-png, heic-to-jpg, webp-to-png, etc.) which preselect the input/output formats.

image-converter.q: Is it safe to convert sensitive images?
image-converter.a: Yes. The images are held in temporary per-request storage inside an isolated Docker container for the conversion pass only — both input and output are unlinked the moment your download begins. Nothing is logged, no thumbnail is kept, no copy is sent to any third-party API. The conversion uses libvips/Pillow locally.
500 MB per file with no daily or monthly quota. Maximum image dimensions are 100 megapixels (about 10000x10000 pixels) — sufficient for full-resolution DSLR RAW conversions.

Format-to-format quality depends on the codec. PNG → PNG, PNG → TIFF: lossless. JPG → PNG, HEIC → PNG: lossless (no re-encoding). JPG → JPG at quality 90+: imperceptibly lossy. JPG → WebP at quality 80: typically indistinguishable. Avoid stacked lossy conversions (JPG → JPG → JPG) which compound artifacts.
No — no account, no email, no sign-up. Upload, convert, download. Privacy guarantees are architectural.

image-converter.q: How is this different from iLovePDF Image Converter or Convertio?
image-converter.a: Free with no daily limit (Convertio caps free use to 100 MB/day), no account required, no watermark on the output, and we support more formats than the freemium converters (HEIC, AVIF, JPEG XL in addition to the standard set). The conversion pipeline is open source and self-hostable.

image-ocr.a: Tesseract handles clean printed text very well (98%+). Handwriting, low-resolution, or low-contrast images are harder.

image-ocr.q: Should I preprocess the image first?
image-ocr.a: Deskew helps a lot for tilted scans. Convert to grayscale doesn't help (Tesseract converts internally).
Tesseract is trained on print. Use a specialized handwriting OCR for cursive.

image-palette.a: We downsize the image to 400×400 for speed, then run a fast octree quantization to find the N most-dominant colors. Percentages are based on pixel coverage.

image-palette.q: Will it find the brand color from a logo?
image-palette.a: Usually yes — logos have a few dominant colors that octree picks up well. For logos on white backgrounds, asking for 6 colors typically gives 1 white + the actual brand colors.

image-palette.q: Can I get more than 24 colors?
image-palette.a: Not in this tool — beyond 24 the palette becomes too noisy to be useful. For full palette analysis, export the image to a design tool.

image-to-pdf.a: JPG, PNG, WebP, BMP, and TIFF. Each image can be up to 500 MB.

image-to-pdf.q: Can I control the page size?
image-to-pdf.a: Yes. Choose A4, Letter, or fit-to-image (where the page matches the image dimensions exactly). You can also set landscape or portrait orientation.

image-to-pdf.q: Are multiple images combined into one PDF?
image-to-pdf.a: Yes. All uploaded images become pages in a single PDF. Drag to reorder them before converting.

image-upscaler.a: The tool uses Lanczos resampling, a high-quality interpolation algorithm that produces sharp, artifact-free results. Choose 2x or 4x enlargement.
JPG, PNG, and WebP images are supported. The output format matches the input — upload a JPG, get a JPG back.

image-upscaler.q: Is there a maximum image size?
image-upscaler.a: The upscaled result cannot exceed 100 megapixels. For a 4x upscale, this means input images up to about 2500x2500 pixels.

image-watermark.q: Can I watermark with an image instead of text?
image-watermark.a: Currently text-only watermarks. Image watermarks (logo overlay) are on the roadmap.

Depends on placement. Watermarks over high-detail areas are harder to remove than over solid backgrounds. AI inpainting tools can sometimes erase them — for stronger protection, use diagonal repeating patterns.
Negligibly. Output is at the same JPEG quality as input.

invert-colors.a: Dark-mode reading on tablets, contrast-flipped scanning of light text on dark backgrounds, or accessibility for users sensitive to bright whites.

invert-colors.q: Will the text still be searchable after?
invert-colors.a: Inverted pages become images, so the text layer is lost. To preserve searchability, OCR the inverted PDF afterwards.

invert-colors.q: Can I invert only certain pages?
invert-colors.a: Currently inversion applies to all pages. Run Extract Pages → Invert → Merge to apply selectively.

jpg-to-bmp.a: BMP is an uncompressed bitmap that legacy Windows apps, embedded systems, and some signage/industrial tools require. JPG→BMP decodes to raw pixels (lossless from the JPG) for maximum compatibility.

jpg-to-bmp.q: Will the BMP be much larger?
jpg-to-bmp.a: Yes — BMP stores every pixel uncompressed, so expect roughly 5–20× the JPG's size.
No. Input and output files are temporary and deleted as soon as the download is returned.

jpg-to-pdf.a: Quality is preserved — JPGs are embedded as-is into the PDF (no re-encoding pass). The PDF wrapper adds about 5% overhead on top of the original JPG sizes. PNG inputs are also embedded losslessly.

jpg-to-pdf.q: Can I reorder the photos before conversion?
jpg-to-pdf.a: Yes — drag the thumbnails to your desired order before clicking Convert. Add page breaks between groups for chapter-style organization.

GPS and camera EXIF metadata are stripped by default for privacy (so the recipient can't see your home location or device model). PDF-level metadata like title and author can be set separately with the Update Metadata tool after conversion.

jpg-to-pdf.q: Is it safe to upload sensitive photos?
jpg-to-pdf.a: Yes. The photos are held in temporary per-request storage inside an isolated Docker container for the conversion pass only — both the input JPGs and the output PDF are unlinked the moment your download begins. Nothing is logged, no thumbnail is kept, no copy is sent to any third-party API. The conversion code is open source.

jpg-to-pdf.q: Can I batch convert dozens of photos at once?
jpg-to-pdf.a: Yes — drop as many as you want into the upload zone. All become pages in a single PDF (drag to reorder before clicking Convert). For very large batches you can split into multiple PDFs or use the Image to PDF generic tool for finer control.

jpg-to-pdf.q: Can I control the page size and orientation?
jpg-to-pdf.a: Yes. Choose A4, Letter, or fit-to-image (where each page matches its source image dimensions exactly). Set landscape or portrait, and pick margin presets (none, small, medium, large) or specify custom margins in millimeters or inches.
500 MB per file with no daily or monthly quota. There is no cap on the number of photos you can combine.

jpg-to-pdf.q: How is this different from iLovePDF or Smallpdf JPG to PDF?
jpg-to-pdf.a: Free with no daily limit (iLovePDF caps free use, Smallpdf restricts to 2 tasks/day), no account required, and no watermark on the output. The conversion code is open source and self-hostable, so you can run it on your own infrastructure if you handle particularly sensitive imagery.

jpg-to-png.a: PNG is lossless — every pixel of the source is preserved. Use PNG when you plan to do further editing (each JPG save degrades the image) or when you need transparency in compositing.
Yes — typically 3–10× larger, because PNG is lossless while JPG is compressed. For photos, JPG is usually a better choice unless you specifically need lossless quality.
Standard EXIF data is preserved when possible. Color profiles (sRGB, Adobe RGB) are written into the PNG header.

jpg-to-tiff.q: Does converting JPG to TIFF improve quality?
jpg-to-tiff.a: No. JPG is already lossy, and TIFF stores those exact pixels without further loss — but it cannot recover detail JPG discarded. Convert when a workflow (archival, print, scanning, OCR) needs a lossless/uncompressed container, not to 'upscale' a JPG.

jpg-to-tiff.q: Why is the TIFF so much larger than the JPG?
jpg-to-tiff.a: TIFF is uncompressed or losslessly compressed, so a 2 MB JPG can become 20–40 MB. That's expected — you trade file size for a lossless, edit- and print-friendly format.
Yes. It runs on the PrivaTools backend with local image libraries (no third-party API); input and output files are deleted immediately after the response.

jpg-to-webp.a: WebP files are typically 25–35% smaller than JPGs at the same visual quality. That speeds up page loads and saves bandwidth, especially for image-heavy sites.
Yes — every major browser supports WebP since 2020 (Chrome, Firefox, Safari 14+, Edge). For maximum compatibility with very old browsers or email clients, use JPG.
It can be either. Our default is lossy WebP for best compression. Lossless WebP is also supported but produces larger files.

json-to-csv-schema.a: Nested keys are flattened with dot notation, such as user.email or billing.address.city.
The tool infers simple column types: empty, boolean, number, date, or string, plus value coverage per column.
No. Parsing, schema inference, and CSV generation all run in your browser.

json-to-pdf.a: Yes. The tool validates the JSON and shows a clear error message with the line number if the syntax is invalid.
Nested objects and arrays are indented with syntax highlighting. Collapsible sections are shown in the preview but expanded in the PDF.

json-to-pdf.q: Can I convert JSON arrays into tables?
json-to-pdf.a: Yes. Arrays of objects with consistent keys are rendered as a table, with keys as column headers and each object as a row.

json-to-yaml.a: Yes. The JSON never leaves your device — pure-browser conversion, no upload.

json-to-yaml.q: Will it format the YAML correctly?
json-to-yaml.a: Yes — proper indentation (2 spaces), keys with special characters get quoted, lists get the bullet-point style by default. Output is ready to paste into a Kubernetes or GitHub Actions file.

json-to-yaml.q: What if the JSON is invalid?
json-to-yaml.a: An error appears in the output area. Fix the JSON and the conversion updates live.

json-xml-formatter.a: Yes — invalid JSON / XML shows an error with the line and column. Common errors (trailing commas, unclosed strings, mismatched tags) are highlighted.
This tool only formats. For conversion, paste into the CSV/JSON converter or use a dedicated converter.

jwt-decoder.q: Is it safe to paste a real production JWT here?
jwt-decoder.a: Yes — decoding happens entirely in your browser using JavaScript's atob(). No part of the token is sent to a server. Verify by checking DevTools → Network.
Not in this tool. Verification requires the issuer's signing key (HMAC secret for HS*, public key for RS*/ES*). The decoder displays the signature for inspection but doesn't validate it.

jwt-decoder.q: What if my JWT is malformed?
jwt-decoder.a: If the three-part dot structure is wrong, you'll see a clear error. If the base64 is malformed, the parser shows which segment failed.

lorem-ipsum.q: Why use Lorem Ipsum and not English?
lorem-ipsum.a: It has roughly Latin letter frequencies so designs feel real, without distracting reviewers with the actual content. English placeholder text always gets read instead of looked at.
Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, and CJK placeholder texts are on the roadmap.
Cicero died in 43 BC. Public domain.

m4a-to-mp3.a: M4A (AAC inside an MP4 container) isn't universally supported — older car stereos, some Android players, and many legacy devices won't play it. MP3 works everywhere.
Slightly. M4A's AAC codec is more efficient than MP3, so at the same bitrate AAC sounds better. Our 192 kbps default produces a result that's indistinguishable from the source for casual listening.

m4a-to-mp3.q: Does it work for iPhone voice memos?
m4a-to-mp3.a: Yes — voice memos export as M4A and convert cleanly to MP3 here.

make-collage.a: Each image is scaled to fit its grid cell while preserving aspect ratio. To force same aspect ratio, crop them first with Resize Crop Image.
Drag in the upload area to reorder. They fill left-to-right, top-to-bottom.
Tested up to 100 images. Output JPEG can be up to 30,000 pixels wide before browser limits.

markdown-html.q: What about extensions like tables and code blocks?
markdown-html.a: GitHub-flavored Markdown extensions are supported in both directions: tables, fenced code, strikethrough, task lists.
Conversion is opinionated — visible content keeps semantics, but custom CSS is stripped. For a faithful HTML→PDF, use the Markdown-to-PDF tool instead.
HTML → Markdown can lose nesting fidelity (deeply-nested divs flatten). Markdown → HTML is exact.

markdown-to-pdf.a: Local image references in the Markdown are inlined if they're in the same upload; remote URLs are fetched at render time.
Not yet — the default style is GitHub-inspired (clean serif body, monospace code). Custom CSS is on the roadmap.

markdown-to-pdf.q: Does it handle code-block syntax highlighting?
markdown-to-pdf.a: Yes — fenced code blocks with language hints get tokenized and colored (Python, JS, SQL, Bash, etc.).

merge-images.a: No — they're scaled to a common dimension (width for vertical, height for horizontal). Smaller images upscale; larger images downscale.

merge-images.q: What if my images have different aspect ratios?
merge-images.a: They get letterboxed (transparent padding) to fit. Use Resize Crop Image first to force a common aspect ratio.
Merge concatenates in a single row or column. Collage arranges in a grid with configurable columns.

merge-pdf.q: How many PDFs can I merge at once?
merge-pdf.a: There is no hard cap on the number of files. Each individual file must be under 500 MB. We routinely handle merges of 30–50 files in one call; if you need more, run the merge twice.

Yes. Existing bookmarks, internal links, and external hyperlinks from every input file are preserved in the merged output. Bookmarks are renamed with a numeric prefix so two PDFs with the same chapter titles don't collide.

merge-pdf.q: Will PrivaTools watermark the merged PDF?
merge-pdf.a: No. The output has zero watermarks, no PrivaTools tag in the metadata, and no header/footer added. iLovePDF and Smallpdf both add a watermark or limit free merges to 2 files; PrivaTools has no such limit.

merge-pdf.q: Is it safe to upload sensitive PDFs to be merged?
merge-pdf.a: Yes. Files enter an isolated Docker container, are processed in temporary per-request storage, and are unlinked the moment the response is delivered. They are never written to permanent storage, never logged, and never used to train any model. The merger code is open source on GitHub.
500 MB per file with no per-day or per-month quota. The merged output can be any size — the only constraint is each input file.

merge-pdf.q: Do I need to create an account to merge PDFs?
merge-pdf.a: No. No account, no email, no sign-up. Drop the files, drag to reorder, click Merge, and download. The privacy guarantees come from the architecture, not from a user profile.

metadata.q: What metadata does a typical PDF carry?
metadata.a: At minimum: producer (the software that created it) and creation date. Often also: author name, original filename, software version. Scanned PDFs may carry scanner model + driver.

metadata.q: Why does this matter for privacy?
metadata.a: Producer + Creator + Author fields can identify the person or machine that created a document — useful in forensics, problematic for whistleblowers.
Yes — both the Info dictionary (old format) and XMP stream (new format) are inspected.

mkv-to-mp4.q: Does MKV to MP4 re-encode the video?
mkv-to-mp4.a: When the MKV's streams are already MP4-compatible (e.g. H.264/H.265 video + AAC audio), PrivaTools remuxes the container without re-encoding — fast and lossless. Incompatible codecs are re-encoded with sensible defaults.
MP4 plays natively on phones, browsers, TVs, and editors; MKV is a flexible container but far less universally supported.
No. Uploaded videos and outputs are temporary and deleted after the response.

mkv-to-webm.a: Often partially — WebM requires VP8/VP9 video and Vorbis/Opus audio, so any stream not already in those codecs is re-encoded. Both are Matroska-based, so the container step itself is straightforward.
To embed open-format video on the web without proprietary codecs.
No — temporary files, deleted after the response.

mov-to-gif.q: How long should the clip be?
mov-to-gif.a: Short — a few seconds. GIF encodes every frame as an image, so a long MOV becomes a very large GIF. Trim before converting.
No — GIF has no audio track. Convert to MP4 or WebM if you need sound.
For short looping clips in chats, docs, and on the web where autoplaying video isn't supported.

mov-to-mkv.a: MKV is a flexible archival container that can hold multiple audio and subtitle tracks. If the MOV's codecs are MKV-compatible, the conversion remuxes losslessly.
When remuxing (same codecs), yes — no quality change, just a different container. Incompatible codecs are re-encoded.
No — temporary input/output, removed after the response.

mov-to-mp4.a: MOV is Apple's QuickTime format. While Macs play it natively, Windows, Android, and most streaming platforms prefer MP4. The codecs inside are often identical (H.264), so conversion is fast and lossless.
Usually no — when streams are compatible, we remux the file (no re-encoding), preserving the original bytes exactly. If re-encoding is needed, we use high-quality settings.
Yes. The audio track (typically AAC) is kept intact.

mov-to-webm.a: WebM (VP9/Opus) is the open format for fast-loading HTML5 video and is well-supported in browsers. MOV→WebM always re-encodes because the codecs differ.
Usually yes — WebM/VP9 is efficient for the web and is often smaller than the source MOV at similar quality.
Yes — local FFmpeg on the PrivaTools backend; files removed after the response.

mp3-to-aac.a: AAC generally sounds better than MP3 at the same bitrate, but transcoding an existing MP3 won't recover lost detail — it just repackages it. Use it for Apple/M4A workflows.
128–256 kbps AAC is typical; AAC is efficient, so 128–192 kbps often matches a higher-bitrate MP3.
Yes — local FFmpeg conversion; files deleted immediately after the response.

mp3-to-flac.q: Does MP3 to FLAC restore lossless quality?
mp3-to-flac.a: No. FLAC will losslessly preserve whatever is in the MP3, but it cannot recreate the detail MP3 already discarded — you get a larger file, not better audio. Convert only when a tool specifically requires a lossless container.

mp3-to-flac.q: When is MP3 to FLAC actually useful?
mp3-to-flac.a: When a workflow or device only accepts FLAC/lossless input, or to archive the file without further generational loss.
No. Uploads and outputs are temporary and deleted after the download.

mp3-to-ogg.q: Will MP3 to OGG sound better?
mp3-to-ogg.a: No — both are lossy, and the source MP3's lost detail can't be recovered. OGG Vorbis can be slightly more efficient at the same bitrate, which is useful for open-format projects and games.
It's a royalty-free, open format favored by game engines (Godot, Unity) and open-source software.
Yes — local FFmpeg on the PrivaTools backend; files removed after the response.

mp3-to-wav.q: Does MP3 to WAV improve sound quality?
mp3-to-wav.a: No. MP3 is lossy; WAV just stores that same audio uncompressed. The detail MP3 removed can't be restored — convert when a DAW, CD-authoring, or editing tool requires uncompressed PCM/WAV input.

mp3-to-wav.q: Why is the WAV file so big?
mp3-to-wav.a: WAV is uncompressed PCM — roughly 10 MB per minute of stereo audio — so a 4 MB MP3 can become around 40 MB.
No. Input and output are temporary and deleted after the download response is sent. Conversion uses FFmpeg server-side.

mp4-to-avi.a: AVI is an older container some legacy editors, players, and devices still require. The conversion re-encodes into an AVI-friendly codec, so expect a larger file than the MP4.
AVI codecs are less efficient than modern H.264/MP4, so files are larger and re-encoding causes minor loss. Use AVI only when something specifically needs it.
No — temporary input/output, removed after the download response.

mp4-to-mov.a: MOV is Apple's QuickTime container, preferred by Final Cut Pro, iMovie, and some macOS/iOS workflows. If the codecs are compatible, the conversion is a fast, lossless remux.
If it remuxes (same codec), no. If re-encoding is required, defaults target compatibility with minimal visible loss.
No — temporary input/output, deleted after the download.

mp4-to-mp3.q: Does this work for any MP4?
mp4-to-mp3.a: Yes — as long as the MP4 has an audio track. Music videos, lecture recordings, podcasts, screen recordings with narration, all work.
MP3 audio is dramatically smaller than the original video. A 1 GB video file typically becomes a 5–15 MB MP3.
No — only the audio track is extracted. If you also need the video, keep the original MP4.

mp4-to-webm.a: WebM uses VP9, which is royalty-free and often produces smaller files than H.264 at the same quality. Ideal for hosting video on the open web.
Every modern desktop browser plays WebM. Safari on iOS supports it from iOS 16 onward. For maximum compatibility, MP4 is still safer.

mp4-to-webm.q: How much smaller will it be?
mp4-to-webm.a: Typically 20–40% smaller than the equivalent MP4 at the same visible quality.

mute-video.a: 100% — we stream-copy the video track without re-encoding. The output is bit-identical to the input minus the audio stream.
Yes, by the size of the audio track. For typical MP4s that's 5-15% smaller. The video portion is unchanged.

mute-video.q: Can I just mute the audio instead of removing it?
mute-video.a: This tool removes the audio track entirely. To replace with silence, use Video Converter and pick MP4 — that will re-encode and let you control audio.

nup.a: Print-industry terminology: '2-up' = 2 pages per sheet, '4-up' = 4 per sheet, etc. Saves paper and ink for review prints.
Original page numbers (rendered on the page) shrink with the page. Add new page numbers afterwards if you need them readable.
2-up and 8-up work well for landscape, 4-up and 9-up for portrait. Mismatches add whitespace around each sub-page.

ocr-pdf.q: What languages does the OCR support?
ocr-pdf.a: PrivaTools ships Tesseract's full language pack: 100+ languages including English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hindi, Russian, Hebrew, Thai, and Vietnamese. Pick the language explicitly for best accuracy; auto-detect works but adds a few seconds.

ocr-pdf.q: Will OCR change how my scanned PDF looks?
ocr-pdf.a: No — the visual page stays pixel-identical to the input. OCR adds an invisible text layer behind the scan so the PDF becomes searchable and copy-pasteable, but the human-readable appearance is unchanged.

Clean 300 DPI scans typically reach 95–99% accuracy on Latin scripts. Lower resolutions or skewed pages drop to 85–95%. For best results, run Deskew PDF before OCR if pages are tilted, and crank up the scanner DPI if you control the scan.

ocr-pdf.q: Can I get the extracted text as a separate file?
ocr-pdf.a: Yes. The default output is a searchable PDF, but you can also download just the extracted text as .txt (per page or combined) or as structured JSON with per-page text and bounding boxes.

ocr-pdf.q: Is it safe to OCR a confidential document?
ocr-pdf.a: Yes. The PDF enters an isolated Docker container, OCR runs in temporary per-request storage, the result is returned, and both the input and output are unlinked immediately. The text is never logged, never indexed, never sent to any third-party API. The whole pipeline is open source for verification.

ocr-pdf.q: Can I OCR a scanned PDF in a language I don't have the keyboard for?
ocr-pdf.a: Yes — the OCR doesn't need a keyboard, only that the language pack is installed (which it is for 100+ languages). After OCR, you can copy the text to a translator like DeepL or Google Translate.

odt-to-pdf.q: What about ODT-specific features (math equations, drawings)?
odt-to-pdf.a: OpenDocument math (Formula) and drawings render correctly as the LibreOffice converter handles them natively.

odt-to-pdf.q: Will fonts that aren't on the server cause problems?
odt-to-pdf.a: Missing fonts get substituted. Embedded fonts in the ODT are honored.
Macros are not executed — only the static document content is converted.

office-to-pdf.a: Word (.doc, .docx), Excel (.xls, .xlsx), PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx), and OpenDocument formats (.odt, .ods, .odp).
Yes. The conversion uses LibreOffice, which preserves charts, images, tables, headers, footers, and most formatting accurately.
Most documents convert in 2-10 seconds. Large files with many images or complex layouts may take up to 30 seconds.

ogg-to-mp3.a: OGG Vorbis isn't supported by some players, car stereos, and editing apps; MP3 is nearly universal. Both are lossy, so this is about compatibility, not quality.
Re-encoding one lossy format to another (transcoding) loses a little quality. Choose 256–320 kbps to keep it minimal.
Yes — local FFmpeg conversion; files deleted immediately after the response.

organize-pages.q: Can I rotate individual pages independently?
organize-pages.a: Yes — each thumbnail has its own rotate button. Rotations are 90° clockwise / counter-clockwise / 180°.

organize-pages.q: How is this different from Extract Pages?
organize-pages.a: Extract keeps a subset in original order. Organize lets you reorder, duplicate, rotate, and delete all in one pass.
Bookmarks targeting deleted pages are removed; targeting reordered pages, they follow to the new position.

overlay.q: What's the difference between overlay and merge?
overlay.a: Merge concatenates files page-by-page. Overlay composites pages on top of each other — useful for adding letterheads, watermarks-from-PDF, or repeating templates.

overlay.q: Can I overlay only some pages?
overlay.a: By default it applies cycle-wise: if the overlay has 3 pages and the base has 10, the overlay repeats. For one-time overlay, use a base + overlay of equal length.
Yes — PDF supports transparency and the overlay's alpha is honored. White rectangles still cover what's beneath; transparent regions show base content through.

page-numbers.q: Can I use Roman numerals or letters?
page-numbers.a: Currently Arabic digits only. Roman / alpha numbering is on the roadmap.

page-numbers.q: How is this different from Bates numbering?
page-numbers.a: Page numbers are simple sequential digits. Bates numbers have a prefix, configurable padding, and are used in legal contexts.

page-numbers.q: Can I start from a specific page?
page-numbers.a: Yes — pages-to-affect lets you specify a starting page (e.g. exclude cover + TOC).

password-generator.a: Length 20 with mixed classes ≈ 130 bits of entropy — uncrackable by brute force. Length 12 ≈ 78 bits — still very strong.
Visual confusion: l vs 1 vs I, 0 vs O. Excluding them makes the password easier to type / read aloud at the cost of slightly less entropy.
Yes — Web Crypto's getRandomValues uses the OS's cryptographically secure RNG (e.g. /dev/urandom on Linux, BCryptGenRandom on Windows).

pdf-page-counter.q: How is this faster than opening each PDF?
pdf-page-counter.a: The tool reads only the PDF's page metadata, not the page content. For 100 PDFs the total scan time is typically under a second.

pdf-page-counter.q: Does it work on encrypted PDFs?
pdf-page-counter.a: Yes for most. Password-protected PDFs that block metadata access return as invalid.
Yes — print shops use this exact tool to count total pages across multi-file print jobs for instant quotes.

pdf-to-bmp.q: Why are BMPs so much larger than PNG?
pdf-to-bmp.a: BMP stores every pixel uncompressed. PNG losslessly compresses to ~20% the size. Use BMP only when you specifically need uncompressed pixel data.
Legacy Windows software that doesn't support modern formats; embedded systems; precise pixel manipulation.

pdf-to-bmp.q: Can I get just one page as BMP?
pdf-to-bmp.a: Extract that page first with Extract Pages, then convert.

pdf-to-epub.q: How accurate is the EPUB compared to the PDF?
pdf-to-epub.a: Text and basic structure transfer well. Complex multi-column layouts, footnotes, and figure captions may need cleanup in calibre.
Yes — embedded images are included as EPUB resources at original resolution.

pdf-to-epub.q: Will the table of contents work?
pdf-to-epub.a: If the PDF has bookmarks, they become the EPUB's TOC. Without bookmarks, the TOC is built from detected headings.

pdf-to-excel.q: Does it convert the entire PDF or just tables?
pdf-to-excel.a: The tool focuses on extracting tabular data. Each detected table becomes a separate sheet in the Excel file. Non-table text (paragraphs, headers, footers) is not included — use PDF to Word or PDF to Text for that.

pdf-to-excel.q: Can I choose which tables to extract?
pdf-to-excel.a: Yes. Select specific pages, or let the tool auto-detect all tables across the document. Auto-detect uses Camelot and Tabula libraries which identify ruled lines and text-alignment patterns.

pdf-to-excel.q: What if my PDF has no visible table borders?
pdf-to-excel.a: The tool can detect tables based on text alignment even without ruled borders, but results are more reliable on clearly bordered tables. For borderless tables with very irregular spacing, manual page selection plus column-position hints in the advanced settings give better accuracy.

pdf-to-excel.q: Is it safe to upload a confidential financial PDF?
pdf-to-excel.a: Yes. The PDF and the generated .xlsx are held in temporary per-request storage inside an isolated Docker container for the conversion pass only — both are unlinked the moment your download begins. Nothing is logged, indexed, or sent to a third-party API. The conversion code is open source on GitHub.
500 MB per file with no daily or monthly quota. Large PDFs with many tables may take 15-30 seconds to extract.

pdf-to-excel.q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
pdf-to-excel.a: Scanned PDFs need OCR first. Run the OCR PDF tool (you can pick the language and deskew the pages), then convert the OCR'd PDF to Excel. The text layer added by OCR is what the table detector reads.

pdf-to-excel.q: Can I batch-convert multiple PDFs to Excel?
pdf-to-excel.a: Yes — upload multiple PDFs and each is converted independently, then bundled into a ZIP of .xlsx files. Useful for processing a folder of monthly statements or invoices.

pdf-to-excel.q: How is this different from Adobe Acrobat PDF to Excel?
pdf-to-excel.a: Comparable accuracy on standard tables. Adobe Acrobat handles complex merged-cell layouts slightly better; PrivaTools is faster, free with no daily limit, and doesn't require an Adobe ID or send your data to Adobe's cloud.

pdf-to-gif.a: GIF's 256-color palette quantizes the page. Text remains readable but gradients and photos show banding. Use PNG for higher quality.

pdf-to-gif.q: Does this make an animated GIF?
pdf-to-gif.a: No — each page is one static GIF. To make a flipbook-style animation, use Video to GIF after converting to images and back.

pdf-to-gif.q: How big are the output files?
pdf-to-gif.a: Typically 30-100 KB per page at 96 DPI.

pdf-to-html.a: PyMuPDF preserves text positioning and fonts via inline styles. Layout is faithful for simple documents; complex multi-column or floating-element layouts may need manual cleanup.
Yes. Embedded images come through as base64-encoded inline data URLs, so the HTML is fully self-contained — no external image files needed.
Web archiving, accessibility (screen readers handle HTML better than complex PDFs), republishing offline documents online, or any use where you need the content as a web page.

pdf-to-image.a: 150 DPI is good for on-screen viewing. Use 300 DPI for printing. Higher values like 600 DPI produce large files but maximum detail.
PNG (lossless, best for text-heavy pages), JPG (smaller files, good for photos), and WebP (modern format with excellent compression).

pdf-to-image.q: Can I convert just specific pages?
pdf-to-image.a: Yes. Enter individual page numbers or ranges (e.g. 1-3, 7) to convert only the pages you need.

pdf-to-jpg.a: JPG is smaller for photos and scanned content (typically 5-10x smaller at quality 85). Use PDF-to-PNG if your PDF has crisp text or graphics where JPEG compression artifacts would show as ringing around letter edges.
JPG doesn't support transparency. White pages render as white; PDF transparent regions become white in JPG. For transparency, use PDF-to-PNG instead.
Roughly 50-100 ms per page at 150 DPI on the server. A 100-page PDF takes ~10 seconds end-to-end. Higher DPI (300+) increases time proportionally.

pdf-to-jpg.q: Is it safe to convert a confidential PDF?
pdf-to-jpg.a: Yes. The PDF and the generated JPGs are held in temporary per-request storage inside an isolated Docker container for the conversion pass only — both are unlinked the moment your download begins. Nothing is logged or sent to any third-party API. The conversion uses PyMuPDF/poppler locally.

96 DPI for web preview/thumbnails, 150 DPI for general on-screen viewing (default), 300 DPI for printable copies, 600 DPI for archival. Higher DPI = larger files. For social-media sharing, 150 DPI is typically more than enough.

pdf-to-jpg.q: Can I convert just specific pages?
pdf-to-jpg.a: Yes. Enter individual page numbers or ranges (e.g. 1-3, 7, 12-15). Each selected page becomes one JPG. Single-page selections return as a single JPG; multi-page selections come as a ZIP.
500 MB per file with no daily or monthly quota. There is no cap on the number of pages — every page becomes one JPG and they're bundled into a ZIP.

pdf-to-jpg.q: How is this different from iLovePDF PDF to JPG?
pdf-to-jpg.a: Free with no daily limit (iLovePDF caps free use to 2 tasks/day), no account required, and no watermark on the output JPGs. The conversion is the same poppler-based pipeline used by Linux distributions, just exposed without a paywall.

pdf-to-markdown.q: How accurate is the structural detection?
pdf-to-markdown.a: Headings work well when source fonts are larger. Tables transfer if cells are clearly separated. Code-block detection is a heuristic — manual review recommended.
Images are extracted to a sibling folder and referenced by Markdown image syntax.
Yes — PDF hyperlinks become Markdown links.

pdf-to-pdfa.q: What is PDF/A and why would I need it?
pdf-to-pdfa.a: PDF/A is an ISO-standardized archival format that ensures documents remain viewable long-term. Government agencies, courts, and archives often require PDF/A submissions.

pdf-to-pdfa.q: What changes does the conversion make?
pdf-to-pdfa.a: The tool embeds all fonts, converts color spaces to sRGB, removes JavaScript and multimedia, and adds the required PDF/A metadata.

pdf-to-pdfa.q: Will the document look different after conversion?
pdf-to-pdfa.a: Visually the document should look the same. Transparency may be flattened in PDF/A-1b, and embedded multimedia will be removed since PDF/A does not allow it.

pdf-to-png.a: PNG is lossless — text and graphics stay crisp. JPG compresses better for photos but introduces compression artifacts on text.
Roughly 200-500 KB per page at 150 DPI for typical text content; up to 2-3 MB at 300 DPI.
PDF transparency layers flatten during rasterization but the result PNG has alpha if the PDF page had transparent regions over the page background.

pdf-to-pptx.q: Will the text be editable in PowerPoint?
pdf-to-pptx.a: The extracted text overlay is editable. The underlying page image stays as a backdrop. For pixel-perfect editing, you may need to remove the backdrop and rebuild from the text.

pdf-to-pptx.q: What about embedded charts and graphics?
pdf-to-pptx.a: They appear as part of the page image. Re-creating editable charts requires manual recreation in PowerPoint.

pdf-to-pptx.q: Can I get one slide per section instead of per page?
pdf-to-pptx.a: Not directly — use Extract Pages to isolate the sections first, then convert.

pdf-to-rtf.a: Rich Text Format opens in every word processor (Word, Pages, LibreOffice, WordPad) without the bloat of .docx and with better text fidelity than .txt. Useful for legacy or cross-platform document exchange.
No. The current implementation focuses on text and structure. For full visual fidelity, use PDF to Word instead.
Yes. Non-ASCII characters are encoded via the standard RTF \uN escape mechanism.

pdf-to-svg.q: What kind of PDFs convert best?
pdf-to-svg.a: Vector PDFs (drawn in Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma, LaTeX, etc.) convert into editable vector SVGs. Scanned/raster PDFs become SVGs containing embedded images.

pdf-to-svg.q: How many SVG files come back?
pdf-to-svg.a: One per page, packaged into a ZIP.

pdf-to-svg.q: Can I edit the SVGs after?
pdf-to-svg.a: Yes. Open in any vector editor (Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma). Text and paths are editable.

pdf-to-text.q: Is formatting preserved in the text output?
pdf-to-text.a: The tool extracts raw text only. Bold, italic, font sizes, and layout are not preserved — you get clean plain text.

pdf-to-text.q: Can I extract text from a specific page range?
pdf-to-text.a: Yes. Specify page numbers or ranges to extract text from only the pages you need.

pdf-to-text.q: How does it handle multi-column layouts?
pdf-to-text.a: The tool reads text in natural reading order. Two-column layouts are generally handled correctly, but complex magazine-style layouts may interleave columns.

pdf-to-tiff.a: TIFF supports lossless compression (LZW, Deflate) and is the format of choice for long-term preservation in libraries and government archives.

pdf-to-tiff.q: Single multi-page TIFF or one per page?
pdf-to-tiff.a: Default is multi-page TIFF for compact archiving. Use the per-page option for compatibility with software that only reads single-page TIFFs.
TIFF is raster only — the text layer is lost. Use Sanitize PDF or PDF/A for archive while keeping text searchable.

pdf-to-word.q: How accurate is the PDF to Word conversion?
pdf-to-word.a: Text, paragraphs, images, headings, and simple tables convert with high fidelity. Multi-column magazine layouts and heavily-designed PDFs with overlapping text and graphics may need light cleanup in Word. Forms convert to plain text — not editable Word form fields.

pdf-to-word.q: Can I convert scanned PDFs to Word?
pdf-to-word.a: Yes. Scanned PDFs are auto-detected and pushed through Tesseract OCR before text extraction. For best results on poor scans, run the dedicated OCR PDF tool first (you can pick the language and deskew the pages), then convert the OCR'd PDF to Word.

pdf-to-word.q: What Word format is produced — .doc or .docx?
pdf-to-word.a: .docx (Office Open XML). Compatible with Microsoft Word 2007 and later, Google Docs, LibreOffice Writer, Apple Pages, and every modern word processor. Older .doc binary format is not produced because it has been deprecated since 2007.

pdf-to-word.q: Is it safe to convert a confidential PDF here?
pdf-to-word.a: Yes. The PDF and the generated .docx are held in a temp directory inside an isolated container for the duration of the request only — both are unlinked the moment the response is delivered. No copy remains in permanent storage, logs, or backups. The conversion code is open source under MIT for end-to-end audit.

pdf-to-word.q: Will fonts and exact spacing be preserved?
pdf-to-word.a: Most common fonts are preserved by name; if Word doesn't have the exact font, it substitutes a similar one. Line and paragraph spacing is preserved to within a few pixels. For pixel-perfect re-typesetting, use PDF to RTF instead.

pdf-to-word.q: How does this compare to Adobe Acrobat PDF to Word?
pdf-to-word.a: Quality is comparable for typical office documents. Adobe is slightly better on multi-column magazine layouts; PrivaTools is faster, free with no daily limit, and doesn't require an Adobe ID. We don't store the file or send it to any third-party API.

pdfa-validator.q: What is PDF/A and why does it matter?
pdfa-validator.a: PDF/A is an ISO standard for long-term archival. It requires self-contained PDFs (all fonts embedded, no external scripts, no encryption) so the document will render identically in 50 years.

pdfa-validator.q: What's the difference between PDF/A-1, A-2, A-3?
